plain: The power to reject a law or decision.

webster.text: A forbidding; prohibition; or the right of forbidding; applied to the right of a king or other magistrate or officer to withhold his assent to the enactment of a law, or the passing of a decree.

example.quote: As the Executive is to have a kind of veto on the laws, and there is an essential difference of interests between the N. & S.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, July 24, 1787
